children: , the jet-engine maker, plans to spend $225 million upgrading its research center in Niskayuna, New York. Shares rose about 0.9% to $322.71 at 11.59am ET time on Friday.

About $150 million will go toward the site itself, with roughly $75 million for research equipment and technology. GE says the work will support projects spanning AI, robotics, advanced materials and aircraft propulsion, while adding 75 jobs over five years. State and local incentives total $13.7 million. American Machinist reports that the upgrade also supports federally backed aerospace research.

A better lab will not lift earnings on its own. The payoff comes if GE turns that research into engines that perform better, production that costs less, or technology customers will buy. At $322.71, the stock stands 19.86% above its $269.24 GF Valuea gap that puts more pressure on those future gains to show up in the business.

title: GE Aerospace Stock Gains as $225 Million Funds Physical AI
